newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C.BANK CHIEF SEES FEWER BANKS-NEWSPAPER.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK CHIEF SEES FEWER BANKS-NEWSPAPER.

text.p: Central bank chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas believes that six to eight banks will remain by the end of 1997 and this number would later fall to four, he told newspaper Verslo Zinios in an interview published on Wednesday.
"My feeling is that the number of banks should decrease this year...since smaller banks will have to merge to survive," he told the newspaper.
"Some six to eight should remain (this year) and some time later the four biggest," Sharkinas added.
Sharkinas said that at least two branches of foreign banks would open in Vilnius before the end of the year.
French Societe Generale has already been mentioned as a possible to open a bank in Lithuania and has visited Vilnius but Sharkinas did not mention other names.
Sharkinas also said he expected banks to boost their capital and be able to compete with banks of neighbouring countries.
He also said he expected the successful sale of two state banks, Agricultural Bank and Lithuanian Commercial Bank, and was pleased Lithuanian banks would take part in the selloff.
Sharkinas also said that for the first time all Lithuanian banks have been audited according to international standards.
"For the first time the Bank of Lithuania inspected all the operating banks in the country and is better than ever aware of the situation in the sector," Sharkinas said.
He also said the central bank was finishing its work on the new law of the Bank of Lithuania which would meet all the requirements of the European Union (EU).
